title: Zoobin
statement:
The city zoo is currently undergoing significant renovations. To improve both visitor experience and animal welfare, the zookeeping staff have opted to reorganize certain animal habitats.

The zoo is organized as a network of enclosures connected by designated paths, with no additional space available. Animals cannot be swapped between enclosures because they would disrupt each other if they used the same path. To resolve this, the zookeeper developed a rotational strategy known as the "zoobin approach," where all animals are moved simultaneously to their subsequent locations around a simple loop (cycle). This method ensures that each animal arrives at its intended enclosure without crossing paths or creating confusion.

Now given the initial layout of the zoo and an expected layout, find the minimum such rotations required to move the animals to their expected places.
inputFormat:
• First Line consists of Integer E representing the total paths connecting enclosures
• Next E lines will contain two integers A and B separated by space representing the paths between enclosure A and B, of current layout
• Next E lines will contain two integers A and B separated by space representing the paths between enclosure A and B, of Expected layout
outputFormat: Single integer representing minimum rotation required to achieve the expected layout.
constraints: Number of simple loops present * E <= 50

sampleCases.explanation: 3 rotations along outer 6-cycle shift the attached spoke to position 2.
